source_cards.front: What makes a child safety seat the best choice, and where can families find low-cost seats?
source_cards.back: The best child seat is one used on every ride that fits your car and has a comfortable harness or shield, and low-cost rentals are often offered by local groups, hospitals and health departments.

source_cards.front: What must a driver do for every passenger under sixteen?
source_cards.back: A driver carrying any passenger under sixteen must make sure each one is secured in a child restraint or seat belt meeting the federal standards in force when it was made.

source_cards.front: How long should a child use a booster seat, and how should the adult belt fit?

needs.title: Seat belt fit and placement

source_cards.front: Do air bags or automatic shoulder harnesses replace the need for a lap belt?
source_cards.back: Seat belts are still required in vehicles with air bags, and if the vehicle has automatic shoulder harnesses the lap belt must also be worn.

source_cards.back: Air bags never excuse the seat belt, and a vehicle with an automatic shoulder harness still requires the lap belt to be fastened.

source_cards.front: When may a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds use a lap belt alone?
source_cards.back: If no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint, a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds may ride with a properly fitted lap belt alone.

source_cards.back: A lap belt alone is allowed for a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint.

source_cards.front: How long should a child use a booster seat, and how should the adult belt fit?

source_cards.front: How should the lap and shoulder belts be positioned with air bags?
source_cards.back: Air bags only supplement belts: wear the lap belt under the abdomen and low on the hips, and the shoulder belt over the collarbone, away from the neck and across the breastbone.

source_cards.front: When must you stop for a school bus, and how long must you stay stopped?
source_cards.back: When a school bus shows its mechanical stop arm or flashing red lights to load or unload, approaching drivers must stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus begins moving.

source_cards.front: Does the school bus stop end once the children have crossed?
source_cards.back: The school bus stop applies whenever the stop arm is out or the red lights flash, and it lasts until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus moves again, not just until the children have crossed.

source_cards.front: On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, who must stop for a school bus?
source_cards.back: On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, only the traffic behind a stopped school bus has to stop.

source_cards.front: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, who must stop for a school bus?
source_cards.back: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic following the school bus must stop.

source_cards.front: What is hydroplaning, and how early can it start?
source_cards.back: Hydroplaning happens when a thin layer of water lifts the tires off the road, and it can begin at speeds as low as thirty miles per hour in water just over one eighth inch deep.

source_cards.front: What should you do if your car hydroplanes?
source_cards.back: If you hydroplane, lift your foot off the gas, do not brake, keep the wheel straight and let the car slow until the tires grip again.

source_cards.back: Hydroplaning can start at about thirty miles per hour in water just over one eighth inch deep, and the response is to ease off the gas without braking.

source_cards.back: A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What should you do at a circular yellow light?
source_cards.back: A circular yellow light warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through.

source_cards.front: Should you speed up on a yellow light to beat the red?
source_cards.back: Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red.

source_cards.back: A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points.

source_cards.back: A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn.

source_cards.front: What does a red arrow mean?

source_cards.front: How does a circular red differ from a red arrow for turning?

source_cards.front: What does a yellow arrow warn you about?
source_cards.back: A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow.

source_cards.front: How does a circular yellow differ from a yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end.

needs.title: Passing and no-passing situations

source_cards.front: How should you pass a bicyclist, and what is the safest way?
source_cards.back: Pass a bicyclist only with plenty of clearance and no oncoming traffic in the other lane; changing lanes is the safest way to pass.

source_cards.front: Which laws govern passing a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: Passing a bicyclist lawfully means following the same vehicle passing laws that apply to passing any other vehicle.

source_cards.front: How much clear road may passing a trailer and its towing vehicle take?
source_cards.back: Passing a trailer and its towing vehicle safely can take a half mile of clear road.

source_cards.front: What two facts should you remember about passing and braking near a trailer?
source_cards.back: Passing a vehicle towing a trailer may need a half mile of clear road, and braking hard near it risks a jackknife.

source_cards.front: How do you pass a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: A motorcycle is entitled to its full lane, so pass it by changing lanes exactly as you would for a larger vehicle.

source_cards.front: How does passing a motorcycle differ from passing a moped?
source_cards.back: To pass a motorcycle you change lanes because it owns its full lane, while to pass a moped you keep at least two feet to its left.

source_cards.front: Why leave extra room when passing any cyclist?
source_cards.back: Leave enough room when passing any cyclist so your vehicle's windstream cannot make the rider lose control.

source_cards.front: What lights must a bicycle have at night, and how far must they be visible?
source_cards.back: At night a bicycle must have a front light visible from at least three hundred feet and a rear red light or reflector visible from at least two hundred feet.

source_cards.front: How do the front and rear bicycle light distances differ?
source_cards.back: A bicycle at night needs a front light seen from three hundred feet but a rear red light or reflector seen from only two hundred feet.

source_cards.front: Why does a truck need extra room to turn, and what should you check before passing?
source_cards.back: A truck's rear wheels do not follow its front wheels, so it needs extra room to turn; check its turn signal before passing a truck that seems to start a left turn.

source_cards.front: When should you look especially for motorcycles and mopeds?
source_cards.back: Motorcycles and mopeds can be completely hidden in blind spots, so look for them before turning, changing lanes or pulling out, especially when turning left.
